subject: Plotting   baseball pitches as  qualitative variable by color.

messages.author: 782ed6ec348dba9b
messages.subject: Plotting   baseball pitches as  qualitative variable by color.
parts:
Hi
First day with ggplot2, second day with R so excuse my lack of
knowledge
I have a dataset (pitches) of baseball pitches identified by
'pitchNumber' and 'outcome' e.g S = swinging strike, B = ball, H= hit
etc.

e.g.

1 B
2 H
3 S
4 S
5 X
6 B etc.

All I want to do is have a graph that plots them in a line cf BHSSXB
but replacing the letter with a color, with a legend, and optionally
having the pitch number above the color

Any suggestion on how to implement this much appreciated


TIA

messages.author: a5679449d442e116
messages.subject: Re: Plotting baseball pitches as qualitative variable by color.
parts:
TIA,

I'm not exactly sure what you are looking for from your description,
but it sounds like you want points of different colors (depending on
outcome) arranged along the x-axis in order of pitchNumber (with all
points at the same y location).

The following R code should do this:
# Your example data in a data.frame
pitchdata <- data.frame(pitchNumber=seq(1,6),
outcome=c('B','H','S','S','X','B'))
# First setup ggplot by assigning the data source and the aesthetic
mappings
ggplot(data=pitchdata, mapping=aes(x=pitchNumber, y=0,
colour=outcome)) +
# Use geom_point to create points (adjust size parameter to control
size of points)
geom_point(size=I(10)) +
# Use geom_text to create labels
geom_text(mapping=aes(label=pitchNumber), colour="black", size=I(6),
y=0.1) +
# Prevent x and y axes from being displayed by setting breaks=NA
scale_y_continuous(name="",breaks=NA) +
scale_x_continuous(name="Pitches", breaks=NA) +
# Setup colour scale (can replace scale_colour_brewer with
scale_colour_manual to set your own colors)
scale_colour_brewer(name="Pitch Outcome", palette="Dark2") +
# Remove grey background from default theme
opts(panel.background=theme_blank())

Hope that is helpful. Let me know if this is not along the lines of
what you were looking for.

Josh.
